stories.headline: Agent authority starts with four operating questions

source.title: Axios CEO newsletter: Reining in AI agents
source.scope: Reviewed the complete Axios CEO newsletter and its four-question framework for agent identity, control, monitoring and auditability, including executive accountability context and practical operating implications.
source.freshness_reason: Within 24 hours at research time; selected for a distinct reusable noncoding authority review grounded in a current executive interview.

read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete Axios CEO newsletter and its four-question framework for agent identity, control, monitoring and auditability, including executive accountability context and practical operating implications.

stories.summary: Axios presents a four-question framework for leaders deploying agents: identify each agent, define who controls it, monitor what it does and preserve an auditable record. The framework turns broad accountability concerns into operating questions. It does not certify any system, but it gives nontechnical owners a repeatable review before granting authority.
stories.why_it_matters: Before an agent acts, write its identity, owner, permitted decisions and stop authority. Define monitoring signals and preserve action records, then have a process owner test one exception. Do not expand scope until every question has an evidenced answer.
stories.related_coverage: Broader agent-governance discovery; complete current executive framework reviewed.
stories.image_alt_intent: Four connected checkpoints label an agent’s identity, controlling owner, monitoring signals and auditable action record before authority expands.

audience_fit.intended_user: Executives, process owners and general knowledge workers deciding whether an everyday agent should receive operational authority.
audience_fit.practical_action: Document the agent identity, controlling owner, permitted actions, monitoring signals, stop authority and retained audit record.
audience_fit.review_action: A process owner tests one exception and verifies the record before approving any additional decisions or system access.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A reusable authority worksheet makes ownership, limits, monitoring and evidence explicit before the agent’s scope expands.

stories.agent_skills_evidence: Reusable noncoding procedure: identify the agent and accountable owner, define permitted decisions and stop authority, specify monitoring signals, preserve an auditable action record, test one exception, and expand scope only after every question has evidenced answers.
